edges.effect_quant: In a 12-week randomized placebo-controlled trial of 200 adults with diarrhea-predominant IBS, heat-treated Bifidobacterium longum CECT 7347 reduced IBS-SSS by 177.60 points from baseline versus 60.44 points with placebo at day 84 (p<0.0001); in a separate 8-week pilot study of 60 adults with mild-to-moderate digestive symptoms, the same heat-treated strain produced only minimal changes in total GSRS-IBS and IBS-SSS scores.
edges.population: adults with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome or mild-to-moderate digestive symptoms exposed to heat-treated bacterial preparations
edges.mechanism: Heat-killed microbial preparations may retain immunomodulatory cell-wall and metabolite signals that dampen visceral hypersensitivity, low-grade inflammation, and dysregulated gut-brain signaling without requiring live colonization.
edges.summary: The postbiotic story in IBS is still early, but there is now direct randomized evidence that at least one heat-treated Bifidobacterium strain can improve overall symptom severity in IBS-D. The signal looks promising rather than settled, because a smaller digestive-symptom pilot was much less dramatic and the strain-specific evidence base is still thin.
edges.caveats: This edge is highly formulation-specific and should not be generalized to all postbiotics. Most of the positive evidence comes from a single commercial strain in IBS-D, and broader replication across IBS subtypes is still needed.

evidence.notes: A randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of live Bifidobacterium longum CECT 7347 (ES1) and heat-treated Bifidobacterium longum CECT 7347 (HT-ES1) in participants with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome.

Effect of Postbiotic Bifidobacterium longum CECT 7347 on Gastrointestinal Symptoms, Serum Biochemistry, and Intestinal Microbiota in Healthy Adults: A Randomised, Parallel, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Pilot Study.

evidence.citation: SchmulsonM et al 2011 Aliment Pharmacol Ther
evidence.notes: Review article: the treatment of functional abdominal bloating and distension.

new_entities.name: Postbiotics (heat-killed)
new_entities.description: Non-viable microbial preparations or heat-treated bacterial products used as functional gut-directed supplements.
